assertions.text: The repository is a bilingual guide (Chinese README with an English README_EN.md) explaining the 'Vibe Coding' approach to AI-assisted programming.
The guide defines Vibe Coding as collaborative programming where developers describe requirements in natural language and an LLM generates complete runnable code, refined through iterative feedback.
It attributes the Vibe Coding concept to Andrej Karpathy, described as an OpenAI co-founder, introducing it in early 2025.
A troubleshooting section lists common problems with AI-generated code: poor code quality, loss of conversational context, and over-reliance on AI, each with suggested mitigations.

It catalogs AI programming tools across categories including mainstream assistants (GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code), extensions (Cline, Roo Code, Tabnine), no-code builders (Lovable, Bolt.new, v0.dev), and cloud IDEs (Replit, CodeSandbox, Gitpod).
The author states they have no coding background yet built six iOS apps and two open-sourced websites in three months using ChatGPT and Cursor, motivating the guide.
The guide describes a five-step iterative core workflow: natural-language input, AI code generation, execution and observation, feedback and refinement, and an iteration loop.

Best-practice sections advise writing specific prompts that state the tech stack, constraints, and expected results, and developing iteratively in small steps while referencing earlier code for context.
The guide lists underlying LLMs it considers foundational to Vibe Coding, including GPT-4/GPT-4o, Claude Sonnet, and Gemini Pro.
A references section cites academic works on code generation (e.g., Codex evaluation, AlphaCode, CodeGen, Code Llama) plus industry reports and official tool documentation.
Repository development practice: the project is stated to be licensed under Apache License 2.0, with details in a LICENSE file.
Repository development practice: the contribution guide instructs contributors to fork the repo, create a feature branch, commit, push, and open a pull request.
